spec: Decode-tolerance proof. Every vector below is a byte string the reference encoder PRODUCED before the integer-widening rule, when an integer needing an 8-byte CBOR head fell through to a float64 (major type 7, additional info 27). Records anchored under that encoder are immutable, so the only thing that can break them is a decoder that stops understanding them. These bytes are unreachable from the post-the integer-widening rule encoder, which is what stops this file from becoming a self-referential re-recording of current behaviour: nothing here can be regenerated by running the encoder again.
captured: 2026-08-11, two independent sources agreeing byte-for-byte: (1) the pre-fix build of the reference encoder, (2) an independent downstream measurement of the published reference encoder build.

vectors.name: first-float64-value
vectors.doc: 2^32. The first value the pre-fix encoder could not fit in a 4-byte head, and therefore the first it wrote as a float64. Post-fix this same value encodes as 1b0000000100000000; this vector proves the old bytes still read back.

vectors.name: first-float64-value-plus-one
vectors.doc: 2^32 + 1. Guards against a decoder that special-cases only the round boundary value.

vectors.name: max-safe-integer
vectors.doc: 2^53 - 1, the largest integer a JS number represents exactly and the top of this profile's integer value domain.

vectors.name: negative-past-the-4-byte-head
vectors.doc: -(2^32) - 1. The negative side breaks one value further out than the positive side, because major type 1 encodes -1-n.

vectors.name: min-safe-integer
vectors.doc: -(2^53 - 1), the bottom of the integer value domain.

vectors.name: action-time-timestamp
vectors.doc: A real Action.time value in milliseconds since the epoch. This is the case that made the defect universal: every Action ever written carries a timestamp above 2^32, so every anchored envelope contains one of these.

vectors.name: grant-expires-at-timestamp
vectors.doc: A GrantArgs.expiresAt value, a field the delegation grammar declares as an unsigned integer, historically pinned as a float64.

vectors.name: round-timestamp-in-a-map
vectors.doc: A historical timestamp nested inside a map, so the tolerance proof covers a structural position and not only a bare top-level value.
